newsitem.title: USA: Mich. subcommittee recommends $69 mln for roads.
newsitem.headline: Mich. subcommittee recommends $69 mln for roads.

text.p: A Michigan House subcommittee has recommended appropriating $69 million from the state's "rainy day" fund to road repairs for the current fiscal year, a House analyst said.

The House transportation budget subcommittee voted 6-2 Tuesday to recommend approval of the plan, which next goes to the House appropriations committee, transportation committee fiscal analyst Robert Schneider said.
The one-time appropriation would be a first for lawmakers to dip into the fund for transportation purposes, although they have done so for other areas, Schneider said.
Michigan senators have already approved the appropriation from the state's budget stabilization fund, Schneider noted.

If projections hold true, Michigan will have $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion in its rainy day fund at the end of fiscal 1998, Schneider said. The transportation appropriation would take interest, but not principal, from the fund, he said.
